confirmed.title: validateProfile lets a write_mode seat run as an advisor, bypassing the --allow-writes gate entirely in soft/hard mode
confirmed.impact: Config `profiles.soft.advisors: [codex-builder]` (codex-builder from SAMPLE_CONFIG runs `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`) passes validation; a soft/hard run then spawns a sandbox-bypassing writable child with no --allow-writes, no clean-git-tree check, and no proof command — a mode documented as read-only can mutate the repo.
confirmed.fix: In validateProfile, throw if any seat referenced by advisors or final_reviewer has write_mode: true.

verdict.reason: agent-council.mjs:533-535 checks advisors only via requireSeat (existence), and :537-538 the same for final_reviewer, while :557-563 prove the design intent by rejecting write_mode on the reviewer — but only inside the mode==="full" branch (early return :546). The --allow-writes/proof/clean-tree gate assertBuildAllowed (:650-665) is invoked solely under mode==="full" (:183-185), and the spawn path (buildAdvisorInvocation :873 → spawn :943) never consults seat.write_mode; the strict-permission env (:1871) applies only to provider:opencode, not codex. Empirically reproduced: a config with profiles.soft.advisors:[codex-builder] (write_mode:true, `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`) passes --validate-config ("config ok: soft (soft)") and --dry-run shows the initial council phase would spawn that exact sandbox-bypassing command with no --allow-writes, no clean-git-tree check, and no proof command — only advisory prompt text restrains the untrusted child. Write-safety gate bypass in a documented read-only mode → P0.

confirmed.title: Empty mapping value parses as {} instead of null, and the truthy {} defeats the full-mode proof-command gate
confirmed.evidence: parseYamlObject: `if (!next || next.indent <= indent) { object[key] = {}; ... }` (line 1596), while parseYamlArray pushes `values.push(null)` for the same case (line 1637). Downstream: `proof_cmd: profile.proof_cmd || ""` (line 630), `if (!buildProofCommand(options, resolved.profile)) throw new Error("Full mode requires --proof-cmd...")` (line 655), builder runs at line 745 BEFORE `runShellCapture({ command: proofCmd ... })` at line 753 calls `spawnSync(command, {shell: true})` (line 1113).
confirmed.impact:
Config `full:
  mode: full
  proof_cmd:` (empty value, e.g. left as a TODO or `proof_cmd: # fill later`) parses to proof_cmd={} — verified: `deadline_ms:
mode: soft` -> {"deadline_ms":{},...}. {} is truthy, so the "Full mode requires --proof-cmd" gate passes, the writable builder seat runs and modifies the tree, then spawnSync({}) throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE — writes land unverified and the reviewer never runs. YAML says empty value = null, which would have tripped the gate.
confirmed.fix: Set object[key] = null for empty values (matching the array branch) so empty proof_cmd stays falsy.

verdict.reason: scripts/agent-council.mjs:1596 sets object[key]={} for empty YAML values (array branch at 1637 pushes null). Empirically verified: empty `mode:` yields error "invalid mode: [object Object]", and a full-mode config with bare `proof_cmd:` passes --validate-config (exit 0) because validateProfile (524-566) never checks proof_cmd. The truthy {} flows through normalizeProfile:630 and buildProofCommand:1979, so the assertBuildAllowed gate at 655 passes. In runBuildPhase, fenced() (2101, String coercion) doesn't throw, so the writable builder runs at 745 before runShellCapture:753 calls spawnSync({},...) at 1113, which throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE (verified live) — writes land unverified and the reviewer never runs. P1 not P0: --allow-writes and clean-tree gates (651, 659) still hold, so writes are user-authorized; the defeated guarantee is post-write verification.

confirmed.title: Duplicate advisor names pass validation, then runAdvisorPlan's name-keyed Map silently discards one child's output
confirmed.evidence: if (!Array.isArray(profile.advisors) || profile.advisors.length === 0) { throw ... } — no uniqueness check; later `byName.set(advisor.name, result)` (line 1024) and `return advisors.map((advisor) => byName.get(advisor.name))` (line 1033).
confirmed.impact: advisors: [claude-opus, claude-opus] (a plausible copy-paste typo) spawns two children, but the second result overwrites the first in the Map and the phase reports the same result object twice — one advisor's stdout is lost and health counts are wrong, with no error.
confirmed.fix: Reject duplicate seat names in profile.advisors during validateProfile (e.g. compare advisors.length to new Set(advisors).size).

verdict.reason: Live-reproduced: a config with advisors [echo-seat, echo-seat] passes --validate-config (validateProfile at scripts/agent-council.mjs:529-535 checks only non-empty + seat existence, no uniqueness), and a real soft-mode run spawns two children but reports the SAME result object twice — both phase entries show identical stdout 'RUN 72127 0.0742...' (same PID/random), the second child's distinct output is silently lost. Cause: runAdvisorPlan keys results by advisor.name (byName.set at :1024, last-write-wins) and returns byName.get(name) per seat (:1033); buildAdvisorInvocation (:880) gives duplicate seats the same name. Health (buildCouncilHealth :1414-1430) double-counts the survivor (total=2, ok=2), so a failure in the discarded child would be invisible. Severity corrected P1→P2: triggers only on a duplicate-name config typo, valid configs unaffected, no write-safety impact — it is a validation-gap/robustness defect with silent data loss, exactly fixable by the proposed Set-size check in validateProfile.

confirmed.title: No 'error' handler on child.stdin: EPIPE from a stdin-mode seat crashes the entire council process
confirmed.impact: A stdin-mode seat (e.g. sample codex-builder) whose CLI exits before draining stdin — bad flag, auth failure, or the timeout SIGTERM landing mid-write of a >64KB builder prompt (builder prompts embed full extracted council sections) — makes the queued write fail with EPIPE, emitted as an unhandled 'error' event on the stdin socket; Node throws, the whole orchestrator dies mid-run, all in-flight seats' work is lost and their detached children are orphaned. Spawn-ENOENT with a pending stdin write hits the same unhandled stream error path.
confirmed.fix: Attach child.stdin.on("error", () => {}) (or pass a callback to .end) before writing the prompt.

verdict.reason: agent-council.mjs:951 calls child.stdin.end(prompt) with no child.stdin 'error' handler, no .end() callback, and no process-level uncaughtException handler (grep: only child.on('error') at :966 and child.on('close') at :989); path is reachable since prompt_mode:stdin is validated config (:602-603) used by the sample config (:78) and threaded via :863/:882. Empirical repro on Node v26.5.0 with the identical handler set: (a) child exiting before draining a >64KB prompt and (b) the timeout-path SIGTERM (:954-961) landing mid-write both produce an unhandled 'error' (write EPIPE) on the stdin Socket that crashes the parent process (exit 1), killing all in-flight seats. Minor corrections: the spawn-ENOENT sub-claim is wrong on current Node (error routes through child.on('error'), parent survives — verified), and prompts under the 64KB pipe buffer do not trigger EPIPE; the core P1 defect stands as stated.

confirmed.title: gitDiffForReview uses plain `git diff`, so files the builder creates (untracked) or stages never reach the reviewer
confirmed.impact: Full mode starts from a clean tree; if the builder's change is new files only (new module + new test — the common case) or the builder CLI stages/commits its edits, `git diff` prints nothing, the reviewer prompt shows "(empty)" as the current diff, and the review gate approves code it never saw — unreviewed writes pass the full-mode safety gate.
confirmed.fix: Run `git add -N .` (or diff against HEAD plus list untracked via `git status --porcelain`) before capturing the diff.

verdict.reason: scripts/agent-council.mjs:1995-2016 — gitDiffForReview runs only `git diff --stat` + `git diff` (worktree-vs-index, tracked files only; no --cached, no HEAD, no untracked handling, no `add -N`). Reached on the real path: full mode runBuildPhase captures it at 754-756 (and 784 per fix round) and buildReviewerPrompt embeds it as "Current git diff" (1292-1293) with instruction "Review the diff like a contributor PR". The clean-tree gate (assertBuildAllowed, 659-664) runs BEFORE the builder, and gitStatusPorcelain has no other caller — nothing post-build detects untracked or staged files, and no code asserts the diff is non-empty; the verdict is taken solely from the reviewer's stdout (verdictOf, 2027-2039). So a builder change consisting only of new files (or one the builder CLI stages/commits — the builder prompt at 1249-1275 never forbids this) yields a literal "(empty)" diff (line 2012) and the reviewer approves code it never saw. Slightly softened by the reviewer also receiving builder stdout and proof-command output, but those are self-report/test output, not the code — the independent-review guarantee is defeated. P1 stands: gate-verdict integrity broken, but writes occur before review regardless, so not P0 write-safety.

confirmed.title: Detached children plus no SIGINT/SIGTERM handler: Ctrl-C on the council orphans running children, including the writable builder
confirmed.evidence:
detached: process.platform !== "win32",
— every child becomes its own process-group/session leader; the file's only shutdown path is main().catch(...) at line 2137, with no process.on("SIGINT"/"SIGTERM") cleanup and no tracking of live children.
confirmed.impact: User hits Ctrl-C on a stuck full-mode run: the terminal delivers SIGINT only to the foreground group (the orchestrator), which dies; the detached `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` builder is in a different group, never receives the signal, and keeps editing the repository unattended after the user believes the run is cancelled.
confirmed.fix: Track spawned children and install SIGINT/SIGTERM (and uncaught-error) handlers that call terminate() on each live process group before exiting.

verdict.reason: agent-council.mjs:945 spawns every child with detached:true on POSIX (new session leader, no controlling terminal), the builder path runBuildPhase→runAdvisor (lines 735–749) uses the same spawn with seat command `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (line 79), and the file contains zero `process.on` calls — the only shutdown path is main().catch at line 2137. Ctrl-C therefore kills only the orchestrator (default SIGINT disposition); the detached builder never receives the signal, the timeout/terminate timers (lines 954–961) die with the parent, and no guard (assertBuildAllowed lines 650–665 gates launch only) covers mid-run cancellation. P1 not P0: writes were explicitly consented on a clean tree, so this is a cancellation-supervision defect, not an unauthorized write channel.

confirmed.title: Reviewer diff is blind to untracked, staged, and committed builder changes because gitDiffForReview only runs plain `git diff`
confirmed.impact: Builder creates a NEW file (the normal case — even the e2e fixture writes untracked built.txt), or runs `git add`/`git commit`: plain `git diff` shows nothing, so the reviewer prompt's 'Current git diff' section reads '(empty)' and the reviewer must approve/reject on the builder's self-report alone — unseen writes get rubber-stamped as APPROVED.
confirmed.fix: Build the review diff from `git diff HEAD` plus `git status --porcelain` and the contents of untracked files (e.g. via `git add -N` before diffing).

verdict.reason: scripts/agent-council.mjs:1995-2016 runs only plain `git diff`/`git diff --stat` (unstaged tracked changes only); it is called from runBuildPhase at lines 756/784 and injected into the reviewer prompt's "Current git diff" section (line 1292). The clean-tree gate at 659-664 guarantees the pre-build tree is clean, so any new file the builder creates is untracked and invisible to plain `git diff`, as are staged (`git add`) or committed changes — the repo's own e2e fixture (agent-council.e2e.test.mjs:149) writes untracked built.txt, producing a "(empty)" diff for the reviewer. The reviewer, instructed at line 1295 to check out-of-scope edits from the diff, then judges on the builder's self-report plus proof output alone. P1 (not P0): writes are already explicitly gated by --allow-writes; the defect blinds the review safeguard rather than opening an unauthorized write path.

confirmed.title: build-report.json and the parent prompt carry only the round-0 proof result; proofs re-run after fix rounds are discarded
confirmed.evidence:
const nextProof = runShellCapture({ command: proofCmd, ... });  // line 779, loop-local
...
const phase = { health: ..., kind: "build", label: "Build", proof,  // <- initial proof from line 751
  results: [buildResult, reviewerResult, ...fixResults], threadId };
confirmed.impact: Round-0 proof fails (exitCode 1) -> reviewer says REVISE -> builder fix makes proof pass -> reviewer says APPROVED; the persisted phase and the parent prompt's Build Phase JSON still show the FAILING proof, so the parent (instructed at line 1410 to trust builder claims only when 'the proof ... supports them') misjudges the final state; the inverse staleness misreports a broken final tree as proven.
confirmed.fix: Track a `latestProof` variable updated each fix round (or store an array of per-round proofs) and put that in the phase object.

verdict.reason: scripts/agent-council.mjs:751 captures `proof` once before the fix loop; lines 779-783 declare `nextProof` loop-local, pass it only to runReviewer (789), and never reassign `proof`; the phase object (798) and build-report.json (803) persist the round-0 proof, which buildParentPrompt embeds at line 1395 while line 1410 tells the parent to gate builder claims on it. runShellCapture (1111-1128) returns exitCode without throwing, so a failing round-0 proof reaches the fix loop; the loop is reachable in full mode (runBuildPhase called at 229) with the sample full profile's max_fix_rounds: 2 and REVISE verdict (769). Only the final reviewerResult (reassigned at 785) — explicitly untrusted child output — reflects the fresh proof, so the trusted evidence channel is stale in both directions (stale-fail after a successful fix, stale-pass after a fix that broke the tree). P1: core misbehavior of full mode's proof/trust mechanism, not a write-safety breach.

confirmed.title: Builder and fix prompts never request the six required headings, so every real full-mode build phase is scored incomplete
confirmed.evidence: buildBuilderPrompt asks only: "Output requirements:\n- List files changed... End with exactly one line: BUILD: COMPLETE or BUILD: BLOCKED." (lines 1271-1275); buildFixPrompt likewise ends "End with BUILD: COMPLETE or BUILD: BLOCKED." (line 1328). Yet runAdvisor wraps every result in withStructuredOutput (line 997), and buildCouncilHealth counts `incomplete: results.filter((result) => result && !result.extracted.complete).length` (line 1423) over `[buildResult, reviewerResult, ...fixResults]` (line 795).
confirmed.impact: Any full-mode run (e.g. sample codex-builder emitting `--json` JSONL) reports build-phase incomplete>=1 plus all six sections in extracted.missing for builder and every fix round; the parent prompt (lines 1334, 1373) and SKILL.md step 5 tell the parent to treat incomplete sections as problems, so a fully successful build always raises a false alarm. The unit test masks this by making its builder stub emit headings it was never asked for (agent-council.test.mjs line 368, headingCommand).
confirmed.fix: Extract build/fix results with a build-specific schema (BUILD: line + files list) instead of REQUIRED_CHILD_SECTIONS, or exclude write-seat results from the headings incomplete count.

verdict.reason: buildBuilderPrompt (agent-council.mjs:1271-1275) and buildFixPrompt (:1328) never request the six REQUIRED_CHILD_SECTIONS headings (:13-20), yet runAdvisor wraps every result in withStructuredOutput (:920/:974/:997 → extractChildOutput :1466-1496), and runBuildPhase feeds [buildResult, reviewerResult, ...fixResults] into buildCouncilHealth (:795) whose incomplete counts !extracted.complete (:1423); the parent prompt then reports incomplete/extractedMissing (:1334, :1347-1348) and tells the parent to account for incomplete sections (:1406, SKILL.md:80). The unit test masks it: the builder stub emits the headings via headingCommand (agent-council.test.mjs:368). Downgraded to P2 because no control flow depends on extracted.complete — the fix loop gates on the reviewer's VERDICT (:769), the run completes, and the parent also sees the builder's raw stdout, proof output, and reviewer verdict; the defect is a deterministic false-alarm in health metadata, not broken build behavior.

confirmed.title: Parent prompt's Build Phase section drops builder/fix stdout, so the file-change list, deviations, and BUILD: line never reach the parent
confirmed.evidence: buildParentPrompt includes only `results: build.results.map((result) => ({ extracted: result.extracted, name: result.name, status: result.status }))` (lines 1396-1400) — no stdout/stderr. Since the builder emits no headings (see finding 1), its `extracted.sections` are all empty strings. references/architecture.md:152 claims "Raw stdout/stderr are still preserved and fenced in the parent prompt."
confirmed.impact: In every full-mode run the parent is instructed to "treat builder claims as advisory until the proof and reviewer result support them" (line 1410) but is never shown the builder's report at all — only name/status and empty extracted sections — so it cannot audit files changed, deviations, or BUILD: COMPLETE/BLOCKED without leaving the prompt for artifacts.
confirmed.fix: Include fenced builder/fix stdout (truncated) in the Build Phase section of buildParentPrompt, matching the latest-advisor-outputs treatment.

verdict.reason: scripts/agent-council.mjs:1391-1402 maps build.results to only {extracted,name,status} — no stdout/stderr — and `latest` (lines 220-238) is the pre-build advisor phase, so builder output appears nowhere else in the parent prompt. The builder prompt (1271-1275) and fix prompt (1328) demand a headingless report (file list, deviations, BUILD: line), while extractChildOutput (1466-1503) only harvests the six ## headings from REQUIRED_CHILD_SECTIONS (line 13) — so builder/fix extracted.sections are all empty, complete:false, and the file-change list, deviations, and BUILD: COMPLETE/BLOCKED line never reach the parent, which line 1410 nonetheless instructs to weigh 'builder claims'. Doc drift confirmed: references/architecture.md:152 states 'Raw stdout/stderr are still preserved and fenced in the parent prompt' — false for the build phase. Partial mitigation (reviewer's extracted sections and round-0 proof capture do reach the parent; build-report.json exists on disk at line 803) makes the parent degraded rather than blind, but every full-mode run is affected, so P1 holds.

confirmed.title: Full-mode dirty-tree refusal and missing-proof-cmd refusal (2 of the 3 write-safety gates) have no test
confirmed.evidence: The only gate test passes "--proof-cmd" and asserts just /--allow-writes/: `assert.match(result.stderr, /--allow-writes/);`. assertBuildAllowed (agent-council.mjs:650-665) has two more gates with zero coverage: `throw new Error("Full mode requires --proof-cmd or profile.proof_cmd.")` and `Full mode requires a clean git tree before launching a writable builder`.
confirmed.impact: A regression in gitStatusPorcelain or the `if (status)` check keeps the whole suite green while a writable builder (sample config runs `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`) launches on top of uncommitted user work — the exact data-loss scenario the gate exists to prevent.
confirmed.fix: Add two tests: --allow-writes + dirty temp repo (touch a file after git init/commit) expecting /clean git tree/, and --allow-writes without proof-cmd expecting /--proof-cmd/.

verdict.reason: All evidence checks out. assertBuildAllowed (agent-council.mjs:650-665) has exactly three gates: missing --allow-writes (651-653), missing proof command (655-657, "Full mode requires --proof-cmd or profile.proof_cmd."), and dirty tree via gitStatusPorcelain (659-664, "clean git tree"). It is reachable on every full-mode run (agent-council.mjs:183-184, before artifacts are written). Test coverage: the only refusal test (agent-council.test.mjs:269-285) passes --proof-cmd and asserts only /--allow-writes/ — gate 1. Grep across both test files shows zero assertions matching "proof-cmd" refusal or "clean git tree"; the e2e test (agent-council.e2e.test.mjs:13-72) is the happy path only — fresh `git init` repo (clean) with both flags, so it exercises neither refusal. The failure scenario re-derives: if gitStatusPorcelain regressed to return "" (e.g. dropped error check at 1988-1990) or the `if (status)` check were removed, both suites stay green, and the sample-config builder seat really is `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` with write_mode: true (agent-council.mjs:77-80), so a writable bypass-sandbox builder would launch over uncommitted work. P1 stands: the gates work today (not P0), but 2 of 3 write-safety refusals — the tool's data-loss protection — are regression-unprotected, which is core coverage, not polish.

confirmed.title: The VERDICT: REVISE fix-round loop — the most complex full-mode path — is never executed by any test
confirmed.evidence: reviewerCommand() unconditionally ends with `"VERDICT: APPROVED"`; the unit fullConfig reviewer (agent-council.test.mjs:395) is identical. So runBuildPhase's fix loop (agent-council.mjs:767-792), runBuilderFix's `{thread_id}` substitution (`seat.resume_command.map((part) => part.replaceAll("{thread_id}", threadId))`, :854), the missing-resume_command fallback (:833-847), and verdictOf's end-anchored regex `/VERDICT:\s*REVISE\s*$/i` (:2030) all have zero coverage.
confirmed.impact: A break in resume-command substitution, re-proof, or verdict parsing ships green; notably, any reviewer output with trailing text after the VERDICT line makes verdictOf return "" and silently skips all fix rounds — unpinned by any test.
confirmed.fix: Add an e2e variant whose reviewer emits REVISE on round 0 and APPROVED on round 1 (stateful stub via a counter file), asserting the fix-N result names, thread_id-substituted command, and second proof run.

verdict.reason: Every factual claim checks out against the code. (1) The e2e reviewer stub unconditionally ends with "VERDICT: APPROVED" (scripts/agent-council.e2e.test.mjs:203), and the unit fullConfig reviewer is identical (scripts/agent-council.test.mjs:395); grep over all *.test.mjs in the skill shows zero REVISE-verdict emissions (the only "REVISED" hit at test.mjs:172 is a Position heading in a hard-mode critic stub, not a verdict). (2) The fix loop (scripts/agent-council.mjs:766-792) is entered only when verdictOf(reviewerResult.stdout)==="REVISE", so no test reaches runBuilderFix's {thread_id} substitution (:854), the missing-resume_command fallback (:833-847 — reachable, since resume_command is optional and defaults to [] at :615), or the REVISE branch of verdictOf (:2030). (3) The path is production-reachable: the reviewer prompt explicitly instructs "VERDICT: APPROVED or VERDICT: REVISE" (:1316), and no validation forbids REVISE. (4) The trailing-text hazard is real: verdictOf trims then applies end-anchored /VERDICT:\s*REVISE\s*$/i, so any text after the VERDICT line yields "" and silently skips all fix rounds — unpinned by any test. I re-ran `node --test agent-council.test.mjs agent-council.e2e.test.mjs`: all 14 tests pass green without ever executing the fix loop. Severity corrected P1→P2: this is a coverage gap on the highest-stakes write path (regressions would ship green), but nothing currently misbehaves — robustness/drift, not live core misbehavior.

confirmed.title: maxTurns: 1 caps the advisor at one tool-use round trip, making the granted Read/Glob/Grep tools nearly useless and failing silently with exit 0
confirmed.evidence: `allowedTools: options.tools, maxTurns: 1,` — official Agent SDK docs: "maxTurns | number | Maximum agentic turns (tool-use round trips)". collectResult falls back to partial assistant text, and main prints `result || "(no result returned)"` with no non-zero exit.
confirmed.impact: Any repo-analysis task needing more than one batch of reads (the norm) ends with error_max_turns and no result string; the adapter prints partial narration or "(no result returned)" and exits 0, so runAdvisor marks the seat "ok" with incomplete extraction — silent council-quality degradation on every real use.
confirmed.fix: Raise maxTurns to a sensible default (e.g. 15) behind a --max-turns flag, and exit non-zero (or emit a marker) when the query ends without a result message.

verdict.reason: claude-agent-sdk-adapter.mjs:46-47 does pass allowedTools (default Read,Glob,Grep) with maxTurns: 1, and the Agent SDK docs confirm maxTurns = "Maximum agentic turns (tool-use round trips)" — one round trip cannot serve a multi-read repo-analysis task. The silent-failure half is also real: collectResult (lines 120-138) falls back to partial assistant text, main prints `result || "(no result returned)"` (line 55) and exits 0 (exitCode=1 only in the catch, lines 150-153), and agent-council.mjs:1003 marks any exit-0 seat "ok". But the P1 "every real use" impact is refuted by reachability: the adapter is NOT the default claude seat (default is the raw `claude` CLI with no turn cap — references/architecture.md:60,65), no config in the repo wires it (no .agents/agent-council.yaml; sample-config.yaml has no adapter entry; the documented AGENT_COUNCIL_CLAUDE_CMD env var is not consumed anywhere in agent-council.mjs), and the SDK is not installed in this repo (references/sources.md:27) so the adapter fails loudly at import (lines 36-40, exit 1). Real latent defect in an optional opt-in path → P2, not P1.

confirmed.title: disable-model-invocation: true defeats every stated trigger — the agent can never fire the skill when the user says 'council' or 'grill this plan'
confirmed.evidence: Line 3-4: description: "...Use when the user wants a council, several model opinions, a grilled plan, adversarial planning..." followed by "disable-model-invocation: true". Claude 2.1.206 binary: `if(e.disableModelInvocation&&!n)return{reason:"disable_model_invocation",message:...}` — the Skill tool refuses it unless the user typed the name this turn. writing-great-skills SKILL.md L16: with disable-model-invocation "the description becomes human-facing — a one-line summary, trigger lists stripped."

confirmed.title: stripYamlComment treats any unquoted '#' as a comment and lets a stray apostrophe disable stripping — both silently corrupt values

confirmed.impact: Verified: `channel: c#1` -> "c" (YAML: "c#1") — value silently truncated; `note: don't fail # reminder` -> "don't fail # reminder" (YAML: "don't fail") — the comment text leaks into the value because the apostrophe in don't opens a never-closed quote state.
confirmed.fix: Only treat '#' as comment start when at index 0 or preceded by whitespace, and only enter quote state when the quote starts a token.

verdict.reason: agent-council.mjs:1798 strips at any unquoted '#' with no preceding-whitespace check, and :1793 opens quote state on any mid-word apostrophe. P2 stands: robustness defect in user config parsing, but sample/typical configs use double-quoted flow arrays that the quote machine handles correctly.

confirmed.title: Tab (or NBSP) indentation counts as indent 0 and is trimmed away, silently flattening nested blocks instead of erroring

gaps.area: Redaction asymmetry in persisted artifacts: config.resolved.json is carefully redacted but every phase JSON stores raw, uncapped-per-run child stdout/stderr (scripts/agent-council.mjs:205, 2059-2078, artifact writes in runCouncilPhase/build phase)

The SDK adapter got only one drive-by finding despite being untested, effectively unreachable, and carrying its own stdin hang. Windows support is half-built and undeclared. No finding in the confirmed list needed re-litigation; the gaps above are additive."
